issues.t: Automatic transmission goes into limp mode or fails
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on and the van stays stuck in one gear (usually 3rd), shifts harshly, takes several seconds to engage Drive, or eventually loses forward drive altogether.
issues.why: The EuroVan automatic is electronically controlled, and loose connections, a faulty transmission computer or internal wear can all trigger failures, sometimes at fairly low mileage. Hard use on long grades and heavy camper loads adds heat.
issues.next: If the van drops into limp mode, drive gently to a shop and have the transmission codes read before it gets worse. Ask the shop to test the transmission computer too, because a bad computer can ruin a replacement transmission.

issues.t: Plastic radiator fan blades break apart
issues.sym: A sudden bang, loud rattling or heavy vibration from the front of the van, often at highway speed or on a hot climb. The temperature gauge may rise, and broken pieces can knock off belts or cut hoses and wires.
issues.why: The electric radiator and A/C condenser fans use plastic blades that can crack and fly apart, especially with heat and age. Many owners have reported this, and VW sent warning stickers instead of a recall.
issues.next: If you hear a bang or feel new vibration up front, pull over safely and turn the engine off. Do not keep driving if the temperature rises or a belt is damaged; have the fans, radiator and belts inspected and replace both fans if one has failed.

issues.t: Plastic coolant pipes and flanges crack and leak
issues.sym: Puddles of coolant under the van, a sweet smell, the coolant level dropping, or the temperature gauge climbing. Sometimes a pipe lets go with no warning and the engine overheats quickly.
issues.why: The cooling system uses many plastic pipes, flanges and fittings that get brittle with heat and age. Owners most often report failures between about 70,000 and 180,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often and look for white or pink crust around hoses and fittings. If the temperature gauge rises, stop and shut the engine off to protect the head gasket; replace aging plastic cooling parts before a long trip.

issues.t: Timing chain sprocket wears and chain can jump
issues.sym: Rattling from the engine, rough running, or a check engine light for cam/crank timing. In bad cases the chain jumps a tooth and the engine can be damaged.
issues.why: On the 24-valve VR6, the intermediate (balance shaft) sprocket that drives the timing chains can wear early because of soft metal. Worn chains and guides make the problem worse.
issues.next: Get any new engine rattle or timing code checked right away. Replacing the chains, guides and sprocket before the chain jumps costs far less than repairing a damaged engine.

issues.t: Heated seat element overheats and burns the seat
issues.sym: A burning or smoky smell from a front seat with the seat heater on, a hot spot, or scorch marks and holes in the seat fabric. Some owners report seats catching fire.
issues.why: The heating element inside the seat can short out or overheat, burning the cushion or seat back fabric.
issues.next: Turn the seat heater off and stop using it if you smell burning or feel a hot spot. Unplug or disable the heater until a shop replaces the element, and check the seat for damage.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator may need replacing (recall)
issues.sym: There may be no warning sign. A recall notice may arrive in the mail, or the airbag light may come on.
issues.why: The driver frontal airbag inflator module on some 2003 EuroVans, EuroVan Campers and chassis models was recalled (NHTSA 18V-406).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have a VW dealer replace the inflator for free if it is still open.

issues.t: Water pump impeller fails and engine runs hot
issues.sym: The temperature gauge swings up and down or runs hotter than normal, especially under load. There may be little or no heat from the heater, or a coolant leak near the front of the engine.
issues.why: Many VR6 water pumps use a plastic impeller that can crack or slip on its shaft, so coolant does not flow well even though the pump still turns.
issues.next: Do not ignore temperature spikes. Have the cooling system tested, and if the pump is replaced choose a pump with a metal impeller.

issues.t: Coolant temperature sensor causes hard starts
issues.sym: Long cranking before the engine starts, rough or stumbling running when cold, poor fuel economy, or a temperature gauge that reads wrong.
issues.why: The engine computer relies on the coolant temperature sensor. When it fails it sends wrong readings, so the engine gets the wrong fuel mixture.
issues.next: Have the sensor readings checked with a scan tool. The sensor is an inexpensive part and is a common first fix for VR6 hard starting.

issues.sym: A check engine light, flashing check engine light, shaking at idle, loss of power or rough acceleration.
issues.why: VR6 ignition coils can crack or fail internally, and some batches failed early. One weak coil causes misfires on its cylinders.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Have the codes read and the failed coil replaced.

issues.t: Door wiring breaks and windows, locks or mirrors stop working
issues.sym: Power windows, door locks or mirrors on the driver door work only sometimes or not at all. Some owners noticed sparks or smoke from inside the door.
issues.why: The wiring that runs through the hinge area between the body and the door flexes every time the door opens and the insulation cracks over time.
issues.next: Have the wiring boot between the door and body inspected. Damaged wires should be spliced or the harness replaced, which also removes the risk of a short.

issues.t: Sliding door will not latch in cold weather
issues.sym: In freezing weather the sliding side door will not latch or lock, the outside handle sticks, or the door can pop open unless held shut.
issues.why: The sliding door latch mechanism and its cables stiffen or ice up in cold temperatures and stop catching fully.
issues.next: Do not drive with a door that is not fully latched. Have the latch cleaned, lubricated or replaced, and keep the door locked from inside in the meantime.

issues.t: Brakes wear out quickly and squeal
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding when braking, pulsing in the pedal, and pads or rotors needing replacement much sooner than expected.
issues.why: The EuroVan is a heavy van, and campers weigh even more, so the brakes work hard. Owners report short pad and rotor life.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked every oil change and replace pads before they reach the metal. Use quality pads and rotors rated for the van's weight.

issues.t: Fuel leaks at lines or filler neck
issues.sym: A strong raw gas smell around the van or through the vents in hot weather, wet spots under the van, or a check engine light for an evaporative leak.
issues.why: Owners have reported leaks at fuel line connections, a kinked fuel line, and a leaking filler neck valve. Screws from aftermarket accessories under the seat have also punctured the tank.
issues.next: Treat a gas smell as urgent. Park outside away from flames, do not smoke, and have the van towed or driven a short distance to a shop to find the leak.

issues.t: Camper fuel vapor container can be punctured (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell around the van, often near where camping equipment is mounted.
issues.why: On some 1997 EuroVan Campers, a drill bit used while installing the camping equipment could puncture the fuel vapor container.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have a VW dealer inspect and repair it for free.

issues.t: Seat belt buckles and latches break or release
issues.sym: A seat belt latch will not stay fastened, a buckle breaks apart, or a retractor locks and will not pull out. This is most often reported on rear and center seats used for child seats.
issues.why: Plastic buckle parts and latch plates crack with age and use, and some retractors stick.
issues.next: Do not use a seat position whose belt will not latch firmly. Have the buckle or retractor replaced and double-check child seat installation.

issues.t: A/C compressor or blower motor fails
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air, the compressor clicks or makes noise, or the fan stops blowing. A seized compressor can throw the drive belt.
issues.why: The A/C compressor and blower motor work hard in this large van, especially on campers with extra cooling demand.
issues.next: If the compressor seizes or the belt squeals, stop using the A/C and get it checked soon, since a thrown belt can also take out power steering and charging.

issues.t: Child seat anchor instructions were wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The owner's manual instructions for child seat anchorages may be incorrect.
issues.why: VW recalled some 2001 EuroVans because the child restraint anchorage instructions were wrong.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and follow the corrected instructions when installing child seats.

issues.sym: Oil leaking from the front of the engine after an oil change, or a sudden loss of oil.
issues.why: The VR6 uses a plastic oil filter housing that can crack, especially if over-tightened during an oil change.
issues.next: Check under the van after any oil change. If oil is pouring out, shut the engine off right away, since running low on oil destroys the engine.
